_**Agent (auto-smart)**_

The mobile TOC jumped to the wrong spot because two separate click handlers were fighting over the same link. In `assets/js/toc.js`, the anchor handler ran first: it measured the heading's position with the dropdown still open and started a smooth scroll to that coordinate. Then the mobile handler collapsed the dropdown, which removed its height from the document flow *above* the heading, shifting everything up while the scroll was still animating toward the now-stale target. You landed roughly one dropdown-height below the heading, and the longer the TOC, the worse the miss. Desktop was fine because its TOC is a sticky sidebar that never changes the flow.

The fix collapses the panel before measuring, in a single handler:

```36:53:assets/js/toc.js
  const initAnchorLinks = () => {
    const links = document.querySelectorAll('a[href^="#"]:not([href="#"])');
    links.forEach((link) => {
      link.addEventListener("click", (e) => {
        const id = link.getAttribute("href").slice(1);
        const target = document.getElementById(id);
        if (!target) return;
        e.preventDefault();
        collapseMobileToc();
        scrollToElement(target);
```

`initMobileToc` now exposes one `setExpanded` helper that both the toggle button and the anchor path use, so the per-link listener that used to close the panel after the fact is gone — no more dependence on which listener happens to be registered first. The `window.innerWidth < 1024` guard also went away since the panel is `lg:hidden` on desktop and collapsing an already-hidden element is a no-op.

Worth checking on a real device with a long post (the study-techniques one you had open has a deep TOC), since the miss scaled with dropdown height and should now be zero.

## Session close
- Fixed: mobile/tablet TOC dropdown now collapses before measuring, so anchor jumps land on the heading.
- Encode: none
- Open: clean

Both checks pass (the base.css prettier warning is pre-existing — it fails the same way on the unmodified file).

Your sticky header is `py-5` around a 60px logo plus a 1px border, so it renders around 100px tall at every width, but `--header-offset` declares only 80px below the `lg` breakpoint. That's the leftover ~20px: the scroll math was correct, it just aimed at a spot the header was still covering, so the heading you clicked sat hidden behind the navbar on phones and tablets.

Rather than hand-tune the breakpoint numbers, the script now measures the header it actually has to clear:

```18:35:assets/js/toc.js
  /* Measure the live sticky header rather than trusting `--header-offset`: the
     rendered height moves with the logo, brand text wrapping, and an open mobile
     nav menu, and the breakpoint values are only approximations of it. */
  const getHeaderOffset = () => {
    const header = document.querySelector(".header");
    if (header) {
      const { position } = getComputedStyle(header);
      const height = header.getBoundingClientRect().height;
      if ((position === "sticky" || position === "fixed") && height > 0) {
        return Math.round(height) + ANCHOR_GAP;
      }
    }
```

Three details worth knowing. The `sticky`/`fixed` check matters because a header that scrolls away shouldn't be subtracted at all — otherwise you'd overshoot upward instead of undershooting down. The `ANCHOR_GAP` of 12px puts a little air between the navbar and the heading instead of jamming them flush. And the CSS variable stays as the fallback, so the graph toolbar's sticky positioning and native `scroll-padding-top` behavior are untouched.

Since scroll-spy shares this offset, the bolded TOC entry now switches at the same line where the heading clears the header, which should also feel less jumpy while scrolling.
